claims.why_not_priced: The specific thing the market is not holding in view is the size of the base effect. Anyone anchoring on the twenty-day run-up sees a flat stock going into the print; the actual position is a name that has roughly doubled since mid-June and is still 46.68% below its 52-week high, so both the bull and the bear can point at a chart and the crowd has settled on the bull reading. Three consecutive double-digit negative reactions at a September-2025 IPO is the signature of a company whose prints keep landing against expectations that have run ahead of them, and nothing in the capture suggests the pattern has been re-underwritten: there is no sell-side preview, no consensus figure and no company disclosure of any kind in August. The band is very wide and crosses zero because the corpus also carries a genuine positive read-through - CrowdStrike and Okta both reported well in late August and Zscaler reports alongside - and because a 46%-discounted name at 75% realised vol can squeeze hard.
